overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against every record of the explicitly given aTable, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the target table is passed explicitly rather than relying on the default table.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against every record of the default table, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when aTable is omitted; applies to the default table (error if none is set).

constraints: queryArgument is written as {conjunction ;} field comparator value: conjunction joins this call to a preceding QUERY call in the same multi-query sequence and is one of & (AND), | (OR), # (AND EXCEPT); it is omitted on the first/only call of a sequence and defaults to & (AND) if omitted elsewhere.

comparator is one of the symbols = # < > <= >= % (% means "contains keyword"); it can alternatively be passed as its own alphanumeric-expression argument (e.g. a variable holding "#" or "=") instead of embedded in queryArgument, which requires separating every item of the query with semicolons.
field may belong to another table if that table is related to aTable via a One-side automatic or manual relation.

To build a multi-criteria query, call QUERY repeatedly, passing the trailing '*' flag on every call except the last; the final call (no '*') actually executes the accumulated query and updates the current selection.

If queryArgument and '*' are both omitted, QUERY displays the interactive Query editor for aTable instead of running a programmatic query (except when this call is the closing call of a multi-query sequence).

The OK system variable is set to 1 if the query completes normally, or 0 if the user cancels the interactive editor (or, in 'query and lock' mode, if the query encounters at least one locked record, which also updates the LockedSet system set).
_needsReview: The alphanumeric-comparator calling form (field, comparator, and value passed as three separate arguments instead of one queryArgument expression -- see the command's own example 21 and 'Specifying the Query Argument' section) is documented in prose but Stage 1 only extracted the two queryArgument:Expression syntax lines, so it isn't modeled here as its own Overload.
